source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Severe anemia from too few red cells, because polycythemia vera primarily reduces rather than increases red-cell mass.","B":"No vascular complication risk, because increased cell mass lowers viscosity and protects against thrombosis.","C":"Isolated neutropenia, because polycythemia vera selectively suppresses white cells while leaving red-cell mass normal.","D":"Thrombosis, because polycythemia vera is associated with increased blood-cell mass and important clotting risk."}}
source_row.rationale: Polycythemia vera increases the risk of arterial and venous thrombosis through increased cell mass and disease-related hematologic abnormalities; thrombosis is a major driver of morbidity.
source_row.source_detail: Polycythemia vera section describes increased red-cell production/hyperviscosity and clinically important thrombotic complications; therapy aims in part to reduce thrombosis risk. Current NCI PDQ patient treatment summary rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: National Cancer Institute — Chronic Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Treatment
source_row.stem: A client with polycythemia vera asks why the disorder increases the risk of thrombosis. Which explanation is most accurate?
